expected_evidence: geological: YD boundary layer (~12.9 ka) sediment/ice-core sequences across multiple continents tested for platinum/iridium anomalies, magnetic spherules, nanodiamonds, and soot/charcoal 'black mat' horizons — refutation would show these are non-reproducible, geochemically terrestrial/volcanic in origin, or confined to local sites rather than globally synchronous
geological: absence of a confirmed impact crater or ejecta field of appropriate age despite systematic search (e.g., under Greenland ice, seafloor surveys)

material: archaeological site stratigraphy (e.g., Clovis-era North American sites) showing no abrupt catastrophic destruction layer coincident with YD onset, or showing biomass-burning signatures attributable to climate-driven wildfire/human land use rather than impact winter
astronomical: cosmic dust/extraterrestrial particle flux records and crater-search survey data (radar, gravimetric, geophysical) inconsistent with a large bolide impact at 12.9 ka

geological: independent paleoclimate proxies (ice cores, speleothems, lake varves) showing the YD cooling onset pattern is better explained by meltwater/AMOC-shutdown mechanisms than by impact-winter aerosol loading
genetic: megafaunal extinction and human population genetic bottleneck timing not tightly coupled to a single catastrophic event at 12.9 ka

model-prior: published peer-reviewed critiques and failed replication studies of the Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (Firestone et al. 2007 and follow-ups) — this is a real, actively contested scientific literature, not directly retrievable from the evidence text provided, so flagged as low-tier/unverified recollection
oral_tradition: comparative mythology claims linking flood/fire legends to a YD-era impact, which refutation would treat as unsupported or coincidental
response.rationale: The interval (-13000 to -12001) falls squarely in the Younger Dryas onset, so the younger-dryas detectability row is the appropriate anchor. The core evidence needed to adjudicate (refute or support) a cosmic-impact/biomass-burning-impact-winter mechanism is geological (0.65) and astronomical (0.7) — sediment/ice-core boundary layers, geochemical markers, and crater-search data — both of which are relatively well-preserved and have in fact been the subject of extensive, decades-long multi-continent scientific investigation (this is one of the most intensively sampled Quaternary horizons). Material evidence (0.35) from archaeological sites is moderately detectable, while genetic (0.3), linguistic (0.05), oral_tradition (0.1), iconographic (0.1) and textual (0.0, no writing existed then) evidence are largely irrelevant or undetectable for a 13,000-year-old event by nature of the period, not because the refutation claim is weak. Because the dominant relevant channels (geological, astronomical, material) are moderately-to-well detectable and have already been actively searched by real research programs, an absence of confirming impact signatures is informative rather than merely a preservation artifact — supporting that the evidence could plausibly have survived and been assessed. I weight the overall adjustment near 0.6, reflecting strong detectability in the geological/astronomical channels that matter most, tempered by near-zero detectability in textual/linguistic channels irrelevant to a pre-literate period. Note: specific claims about actual published refutation studies (e.g., failed nanodiamond replication, terrestrial platinum sourcing) are drawn from general scientific-literature recall (model-prior), not from the evidence text supplied, and should be treated as unverified pending source confirmation.
